correctness.rationale: Backwards genealogies start at all four sites; the first jump among four distinct ancestral lineages necessarily coalesces at exponential rate 4. Hypergeometric nonconsensus probabilities satisfy q2(j)-(4/3)q1(j)=0 for j=1,2,3 and -1/3 at j=4; integrating P(Jt=4)=e^{-4t} yields -1/12. Complement symmetry gives T3=T1 and positivity of exchangeable coefficient gives universal ordering. The undirected finite table follows from rational 14-state first-step systems for all 38 labeled connected graphs and their 6 isomorphism types. Independent exact rational solver reproduced all 6 graph T1 values and the universal T2 identity; input program enumerates all 38 and all edge transitions.
residual_risks: All copying matrices must have zero diagonal and equal rate-one vertex clocks; a self-copy probability changes first-coalescence law.
Fixed initial law must be exchangeable and independent of clocks; arbitrary deterministic initial states can rank networks differently.

value.rationale: The invariance under arbitrary exchangeable laws is a structural robustness fact for a classical stochastic network model; the sharp n=4 edge-induced slowdown boundary with two explicit transitions resolves a finite graph classification rather than reporting an isolated example.
residual_risks: Different rate conventions or nonexchangeable initial laws invalidate the same numerical constants.

final_claim: For continuous-time four-site zero-diagonal irreducible binary voter copying with equal rate-one clocks, uniform initial k-subset conditional means obey T3=T1 and T2=(4/3)T1-1/12 for all copying matrices. Any nontrivial exchangeable initial law gives the same strict network ordering. For connected simple undirected four-vertex graphs, the exact six T1 values and six edge-insertion increments exhibit exactly two slowdown additions (star to paw and paw to diamond); four sites are the sharp minimum size.
limitations: All copying matrices must have zero diagonal and equal rate-one vertex clocks; a self-copy probability changes first-coalescence law.
Fixed initial law must be exchangeable and independent of clocks; arbitrary deterministic initial states can rank networks differently.
Earlier specialized four-site voter-table results might contain equivalent fractions under another time normalization.
The graph census applies only to connected simple undirected networks; the affine identity covers larger class of directed weighted matrices.
